claim: HGSOC cells in suspension culture show reduced expression of Ki67 compared to adherent culture.
source: Figure 1A illustrates withdrawal from cellular proliferation by HGSOC cells in suspension as evidenced by reduced expression of Ki67
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 1A shows reduced Ki67 levels in spheroid (Sph) conditions compared to adherent (Adh) conditions across three cell lines.

claim: HGSOC cells in suspension culture show increased expression of the quiescence marker p130 compared to adherent culture.
source: Figure 1A illustrates withdrawal from cellular proliferation by HGSOC cells in suspension as evidenced by reduced expression of Ki67 and increased expression of the quiescence marker p130 (Litovchick et al., 2004).
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 1A demonstrates elevated p130 levels in spheroid conditions compared to adherent conditions, and this is supported by citation to Litovchick et al., 2004.

claim: p130 is a quiescence marker.
source: increased expression of the quiescence marker p130 (Litovchick et al., 2004)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Litovchick et al., 2004.

claim: Phospho-ERK levels are reduced but not absent in HGSOC spheroids compared to adherent cells.
source: Furthermore, phospho-western blots for ERK demonstrate reduced but not absent phosphorylation
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 1A shows reduced phospho-ERK levels in spheroid conditions compared to adherent conditions.

claim: Phospho-p38 levels either remain consistent or are increased in HGSOC spheroids compared to adherent cells.
source: and phospho-p38 either remains consistent or is increased
evidence: Western blot data in Figure 1A shows phospho-p38 levels that are similar or elevated in spheroid conditions compared to adherent conditions.

claim: Reduced phospho-ERK and elevated phospho-p38 are indicative of the characteristic signaling switch reported to underlie most paradigms of cancer cell dormancy.
source: Reduced phospho-ERK and elevated phospho-p38 are indicative of the characteristic signaling switch reported to underlie most paradigms of cancer cell dormancy (Goddard et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Goddard et al., 2018.

claim: GO-CRISPR incorporates sgRNA abundances from non-Cas9-expressing cells to control for stochastic effects in three-dimensional culture conditions with slow or arrested proliferation.
source: GO-CRISPR incorporates sgRNA abundances from non-Cas9-expressing cells to control for stochastic (non-Cas9 dependent) effects that are a challenge in three-dimensional culture conditions with slow or arrested proliferation (Zanoni et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript describes the GO-CRISPR method and cites Zanoni et al., 2016 for the challenge of stochastic effects in 3D culture.

claim: Greater than 95% of sgRNAs in iOVCA147 and OVCAR8 screens were classified as non-essential.
source: Greater than 95% of sgRNAs in iOVCA147 and OVCAR8 screens were classified as non-essential
evidence: ROC curve analysis in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C shows area under the curve values indicating high classification accuracy for non-targeting controls.

claim: 83% of sgRNAs in TOV1946 cells were non-essential.
source: while 83% of sgRNAs in TOV1946 cells were non-essential
evidence: ROC curve analysis in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C shows area under the curve value for TOV1946.

claim: There is a statistically significant correlation between GO-CRISPR screen ER values and viability data from siRNA knock down for 35 individual genes in OVCAR8 and iOVCA147 cells.
source: This revealed a statistically significant correlation between the two sets of data, suggesting that genes we previously knew supported spheroid viability (or were dispensable) were classified similarly by our screen.
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 1D shows a scatter plot with linear regression comparing siRNA viability data with GO-CRISPR enrichment ratios, demonstrating correlation.

claim: 6,717 genes with an ER below 1 were found in iOvCa147 cells.
source: We found 6,717 genes with an ER below 1 in iOvCa147 cells
evidence: Figure 1C shows scatter plot with 6,717 genes highlighted for iOvCa147.

claim: 7,637 genes with an ER below 1 were found in TOV1946 cells.
source: and 7,637 genes in TOV1946
evidence: Figure 1C shows scatter plot with 7,637 genes highlighted for TOV1946.

claim: 7,640 genes with an ER below 1 were found in OVCAR8 cells.
source: and 7,640 genes in OVCAR8 cells
evidence: Figure 1C shows scatter plot with 7,640 genes highlighted for OVCAR8.

claim: 1382 genes were common to all three cell lines among those with ER below 1.
source: Among these genes; 1382 were common to all three cell lines (Figure 1D).
evidence: Venn diagram in Figure 1D shows 1382 genes in the intersection of all three cell lines.

claim: Axon guidance is an enriched pathway among the 1382 common genes identified in GO-CRISPR screens.
source: In addition, we identified a tertiary category called 'axon guidance,' that includes numerous components of the Netrin signaling pathway that scored highly.
evidence: Figure 1E shows 'Axon guidance' as one of the enriched pathways from ConsensusPathDB analysis.

claim: DYRK1A was previously discovered to support survival of ovarian cancer cells in suspension culture.
source: DYRK1A was previously discovered to support survival of ovarian cancer cells in suspension culture (MacDonald et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to MacDonald et al., 2017.

claim: DYRK1A phosphorylates RNA polymerase II in transcription initiation.
source: Since DYRK1A phosphorylates RNA polymerase II in transcription initiation (Di Vona et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Di Vona et al., 2015.

claim: DYRK1A-/- iOvCa147 cells are deficient for survival in suspension.
source: We created DYRK1A-/- iOvCa147 cells and confirmed their deficiency for survival in suspension (Figure 2; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–E).
evidence: Figure 2—figure supplement 1E shows reduced viability of DYRK1A-/- cells in suspension culture compared to parental cells.

claim: 1834 genes were upregulated in iOvCa147 spheroid cells compared to adherent cells.
source: We identified 1834 genes that were upregulated
evidence: Figure 2A volcano plot shows 1,834 genes upregulated (log2 fold change >1, padj <0.05, FDR 10%).

claim: Axon guidance is an enriched pathway among genes upregulated in iOvCa147 spheroid cells compared to adherent cells.
source: and pathway enrichment analysis identified many of the same categories as our CRISPR screen including axon guidance (Figure 2B)
evidence: Figure 2B shows 'Axon guidance' among the top 15 enriched pathways for upregulated genes in spheroids.

claim: 744 genes were downregulated in DYRK1A-/- spheroid cells compared to iOvCa147 spheroid cells.
source: We identified 744 genes that were downregulated
evidence: Figure 2C volcano plot shows 744 genes downregulated (log2 fold change <1, padj <0.05, FDR 10%).

claim: Axon guidance is an enriched pathway among genes downregulated in DYRK1A-/- spheroid cells compared to iOvCa147 spheroid cells.
source: and these also belonged to many of the same pathways, including axon guidance (Figure 2D)
evidence: Figure 2D shows 'Axon guidance' among the top 15 enriched pathways for downregulated genes in DYRK1A-/- spheroids.

claim: 78 pathways were commonly enriched across GO-CRISPR screens, upregulated genes in iOvCa147 spheroids, and downregulated genes in DYRK1A-/- spheroids.
source: 78 Reactome pathways were commonly enriched across the GO-CRISPR screens and transcriptomic analyses
evidence: Figure 2E Venn diagram shows 78 pathways in the intersection of all three datasets.

claim: Axon guidance is one of the most enriched pathways among the 78 commonly enriched pathways.
source: The axon guidance pathway was one of the most enriched among these common pathways (Figure 2F).
evidence: Figure 2F shows 'Axon guidance' ranked 8th among the top 10 most significantly enriched pathways.

claim: Each HGSOC cell line (iOvCa147, OVCAR8, TOV1946) increases expression of some Netrins in spheroid culture.
source: The precise identities of upregulated genes varies between cell lines; however, each cell line increases expression of some Netrins
evidence: Figure 3A-C shows RT-qPCR data demonstrating increased expression of various Netrin ligands in suspension culture across the three cell lines.

claim: Each HGSOC cell line increases expression of at least one UNC5 receptor in spheroid culture.
source: at least one UNC5
evidence: Figure 3A-C shows RT-qPCR data demonstrating increased expression of UNC5 receptors in suspension culture across the three cell lines.

claim: Each HGSOC cell line increases expression of at least one of DCC, DSCAM, and Neogenin in spheroid culture.
source: and at least one of DCC, DSCAM, and Neogenin
evidence: Figure 3A-C shows RT-qPCR data demonstrating increased expression of DCC, DSCAM, or Neogenin in suspension culture across the three cell lines.

claim: Solid HGSOC tumors display uniform Ki67 positivity.
source: As expected, solid HGSOC tumors display uniform Ki67 positivity
evidence: Figure 4A-B shows immunohistochemical staining with uniform Ki67 nuclear staining in solid HGSOC tumor sections.

claim: Solid HGSOC tumors display relative absence of p130.
source: and relative absence of p130 (Figure 4A–B)
evidence: Figure 4A-B shows immunohistochemical staining with minimal p130 staining in solid HGSOC tumor sections.

claim: Patient-derived HGSOC spheroids demonstrate rare Ki67 nuclear staining.
source: Conversely, serial sections of spheroids demonstrated rare Ki67 nuclear staining
evidence: Figure 4C-E shows immunohistochemical staining with rare Ki67 positive nuclei in patient-derived spheroid sections.

claim: Patient-derived HGSOC spheroids demonstrate abundant and uniform p130 staining.
source: and abundant and uniform p130 staining
evidence: Figure 4C-E shows immunohistochemical staining with uniform p130 nuclear staining in patient-derived spheroid sections.

claim: Cells in patient-derived HGSOC spheroids are quiescent.
source: This indicates that cells in these patient derived spheroids are quiescent (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the Ki67 and p130 staining patterns shown in Figure 4C-E, which are consistent with quiescence.

claim: Netrin-1 is expressed in dormant patient-derived HGSOC spheroids.
source: Dormant patient derived spheroids were stained for Netrins and epithelial markers Cytokeratin and EpCAM.
evidence: Figure 4F-H shows immunohistochemical staining for Netrin-1 in patient-derived spheroid sections.

claim: Netrin-3 is expressed in dormant patient-derived HGSOC spheroids.
source: Dormant patient derived spheroids were stained for Netrins and epithelial markers Cytokeratin and EpCAM.
evidence: Figure 4F-H shows immunohistochemical staining for Netrin-3 in patient-derived spheroid sections.

claim: Patient-derived HGSOC spheroids express p53 at high levels in the nucleus.
source: Since HGSOC is characterized by point mutations in p53 and its accumulation in the nucleus, sections were also stained for p53 to confirm cancer cell identity within these spheroids by high level nuclear staining (Figure 4F–H).
evidence: Figure 4F-H shows immunohistochemical staining with high level nuclear p53 staining in patient-derived spheroid sections.

claim: Loss of at least one Netrin ligand resulted in reduced spheroid cell survival in five of six HGSOC cell lines.
source: Loss of at least one Netrin ligand resulted in reduced spheroid cell survival in five of six cell lines (Figure 5B).
evidence: Figure 5B bubble plot shows reduced viability for Netrin ligand knockouts in multiple cell lines.

claim: Netrin-3 loss showed the most pronounced effect on spheroid survival.
source: Notably, Netrin-3 loss showed the most pronounced effect on survival.
evidence: Figure 5B bubble plot shows larger bubbles (indicating greater significance) for NTN3 knockouts across multiple cell lines.

claim: OVCAR8 and COV318 cell lines are relatively resistant to deletion of individual Netrin pathway components.
source: Cell lines such as OVCAR8 and COV318 were relatively resistant to the deletion of Netrin pathway components as individual UNC5, DCC, and DSCAM genes rarely affected viability (Figure 5B).
evidence: Figure 5B bubble plot shows smaller or absent bubbles for individual receptor knockouts in OVCAR8 and COV318.

claim: Combined deletions of UNC5 family members or DCC;DSCAM;NEO1 in OVCAR8 and COV318 cells were either inviable or highly sensitive to suspension culture induced cell death.
source: In these instances, combined deletions of UNC5 family members, or DCC;DSCAM;NEO1 (DDN for short) were either inviable or highly sensitive to suspension culture induced cell death
evidence: Figure 5B bubble plot shows large bubbles or empty spaces (indicating inviability) for UNC5 4KO and DDN 3KO in OVCAR8 and COV318.

claim: OVCAR3 cells are highly sensitive to the loss of multiple individual Netrin ligands.
source: Other cell lines, such as OVCAR3, were highly sensitive to the loss of multiple individual ligands
evidence: Figure 5B bubble plot shows large bubbles for multiple Netrin ligand knockouts in OVCAR3.

claim: Loss of any individual UNC5H receptor is highly sensitizing to death induction in suspension in OVCAR3 cells.
source: and any individual UNC5H receptor was highly sensitizing to death induction in suspension (Figure 5B)
evidence: Figure 5B bubble plot shows large bubbles for individual UNC5 receptor knockouts in OVCAR3.

claim: Loss of Netrin receptor expression does not elevate viability in HGSOC spheroids.
source: Importantly, loss of receptor expression does not elevate viability as expected for a dependence receptors
evidence: Figure 5B shows reduced or unchanged viability for receptor knockouts, not increased viability.

claim: Loss of Netrin receptor expression does not induce DAPK1 dephosphorylation in HGSOC spheroids.
source: nor does it induce DAPK1 dephosphorylation (Figure 5; Figure 5—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1D shows western blot with no change in DAPK1 phosphorylation in UNC5 knockout cells.

claim: Netrin receptors in HGSOC spheroids transmit positive survival signals.
source: suggesting that Netrin receptors in HGSOC spheroids transmit positive survival signals
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that receptor loss reduces viability and does not induce pro-death signals.

claim: Netrin-1 stimulates ERK phosphorylation in HGSOC spheroid cultures.
source: Western blotting for phospho-ERK, as a measure of activation, revealed stimulation of MEK-ERK signaling in each of the cell lines tested.
evidence: Figure 5C shows western blots with increased phospho-ERK levels after Netrin-1 stimulation in spheroid cultures across multiple cell lines.

claim: Netrin-1 is only able to stimulate ERK phosphorylation in suspension culture, not in quiescent adherent cells.
source: Both conditions display similar, low levels of phospho-ERK, but Netrin-1 was only able to stimulate ERK phosphorylation in suspension (Figure 5D).
evidence: Figure 5D shows western blots comparing Netrin-1 stimulation in adherent vs. suspension culture, with ERK phosphorylation only occurring in suspension.

claim: EGF induces pERK levels commonly seen in proliferating cells when applied to adherent cells.
source: Importantly, stimulation of adherent cells with an equivalent concentration of EGF induced pERK levels commonly seen in proliferating cells.
evidence: Figure 5D shows western blot with high phospho-ERK levels after EGF stimulation in adherent cells.

claim: The context and magnitude of pERK stimulation by Netrin-1 is inconsistent with proliferative signaling.
source: Collectively, the context and magnitude of pERK stimulation by Netrin-1 is inconsistent with proliferative signaling, suggesting it may contribute to survival.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the low level ERK phosphorylation by Netrin-1 in spheroids with the high level ERK phosphorylation by EGF in proliferating cells.

claim: ERK phosphorylation is lower in HGSOC spheroids when UNC5H and DDN receptors are deleted.
source: We investigated the dependence of ERK phosphorylation on UNC5H and DDN receptors and discovered that it is lower when receptors are deleted (Figure 5E).
evidence: Figure 5E shows western blots with reduced phospho-ERK levels in UNC5 4KO and DDN 3KO cells compared to control.

claim: Netrin receptors are essential to activate ERK in suspension culture.
source: Furthermore, Netrin-1 stimulation of suspension cultures of OVCAR8 cells, or derivatives deleted for UNC5 family members or DDN receptors, indicated that Netrin receptors are essential to activate ERK in suspension culture (Figure 5F).
evidence: Figure 5F shows western blots where Netrin-1 stimulation increases phospho-ERK in control cells but not in UNC5 4KO or DDN 3KO cells.

claim: MEK inhibitors PD184352 and Trametinib cause loss of cell viability in OVCAR8 suspension cultures.
source: To confirm that Netrin-MEK-ERK signaling contributes to survival in suspension culture, we used two different MEK inhibitors, PD184352 and Trametinib, to treat OVCAR8 suspension cultures and observed that it causes loss of cell viability in suspension culture (Figure 5G).
evidence: Figure 5G shows reduced viability in OVCAR8 spheroids treated with PD184352 or Trametinib compared to DMSO control.

claim: Trametinib kills OVCAR8 cells in suspension culture as measured by trypan blue dye exclusion.
source: Since we routinely use reattachment of spheroids to adherent plastic as a test of viability, also tested viability using trypan blue dye exclusion to confirm that Trametinib is truly killing cells in suspension and it revealed the same conclusion (Figure 5H).
evidence: Figure 5H shows reduced viability by trypan blue dye exclusion in OVCAR8 spheroids treated with Trametinib compared to DMSO control.

claim: Treatment of OVCAR8 cells in suspension with Trametinib leads to lower phospho-ERK levels.
source: As expected, treatment of cells in suspension with Trametinib lead to lower phospho-ERK levels (Figure 5I).
evidence: Figure 5I shows western blot with reduced phospho-ERK levels in Trametinib treated spheroids compared to DMSO control.

claim: Netrins signal through a heterodimer or multi-receptor complex containing both an UNC5 and DDN component to provide low level stimulation for MEK and ERK in dormant culture conditions.
source: The simplest explanation of this data is that Netrins signal through a heterodimer or multi-receptor complex containing both an UNC5 and DDN component that provides low level stimulation for MEK and ERK specifically in dormant culture conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both UNC5 and DDN receptor families are required for Netrin-stimulated ERK phosphorylation in spheroids.

claim: Spheroids recovered from abdominal washes two weeks post-engraftment show reduced expression of pro-proliferative genes compared to cells prior to engraftment.
source: Extraction of RNA from control OVCAR8 cell spheroids recovered at this time point indicates a reduction in expression of pro-proliferative genes compared to the same cells prior to engraftment (Figure 6B).
evidence: Figure 6B shows RT-qPCR data with reduced expression of Ki67, Cyclin D1, and PCNA in spheroids from xenografts compared to pre-engraftment cells.

claim: Spheroids from abdominal washes are equivalently withdrawn from the cell cycle as suspension culture induced spheroids.
source: Furthermore, comparison with RT-qPCR measurements of these same markers in suspension culture induced OVCAR8 spheroids indicates that spheroids from abdominal washes are equivalently withdrawn from the cell cycle (Figure 6; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1 show similar levels of cell cycle marker expression in spheroids from xenografts and suspension culture.

claim: Spheroids at two weeks post-engraftment are dormant.
source: This suggests spheroids at this stage are dormant.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced expression of proliferative markers and similarity to suspension culture spheroids.

claim: Deletion of UNC5 receptors extensively reduces survival of OVCAR8 spheroids in xenografts at two weeks post-engraftment.
source: Furthermore, recovery of spheroids by replating on adherent plastic indicates that deletion of UNC5 receptors to block Netrin signaling extensively reduces survival under these circumstances (Figure 6C).
evidence: Figure 6C shows reduced crystal violet staining and biomass in UNC5 4KO spheroids compared to control spheroids recovered from xenografts.

claim: Cancer cell abundance is reduced in the dormant state by loss of UNC5 receptors as measured by human Alu repeat detection.
source: We also quantitated cancer cells in these abdominal washes by qPCR using human Alu repeat detection to count cells and this also demonstrates that cancer cell abundance is reduced in this dormant state by loss of UNC5 receptors.
evidence: Figure 6D shows reduced human Alu repeat detection in abdominal washes from mice engrafted with UNC5 4KO cells compared to control.

claim: Mice engrafted with UNC5 4KO cells have considerably longer survival than control OVCAR8 recipient mice.
source: This demonstrated that mice engrafted with UNC5 4KO cells had a considerably longer survival than control OVCAR8 recipient mice that received the same number of cells (Figure 6E and F).
evidence: Figure 6F shows Kaplan-Meier survival curves with significantly longer survival for mice engrafted with UNC5 4KO cells compared to control (logrank test).

claim: Inhibition of Netrin signaling compromises viability and eventual disease progression in a model of dormancy and dissemination.
source: Collectively, this demonstrates that inhibition of Netrin signaling compromises viability and eventual disease progression in a model of dormancy and dissemination.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced spheroid survival and extended mouse survival observed with UNC5 receptor deletion.

claim: HGSOC is one of the most aneuploid cancers.
source: Genomic studies indicate that HGSOC is one of the most aneuploid cancers (Network CGA, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Network CGA, 2011.

claim: TCGA genomic data for HGSOC indicates rare amplifications or deletions of Netrin or Netrin-receptor genes.
source: Evaluation of TCGA genomic data for HGSOC indicates rare amplifications or deletions of Netrin or Netrin-receptor genes (Figure 7; Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Figure 7—figure supplement 1A shows oncoprint with infrequent genetic alterations in Netrin pathway genes.

claim: HGSOC cases with deficiency for Netrin signaling are rare.
source: Because of redundancy of Netrins and their receptor families this data suggests HGSOC cases with deficiency for Netrin signaling are rare.
evidence: This is inferred from the rare deletions of Netrin pathway genes and the redundancy of the pathway.

claim: Some TCGA HGSOC cases display elevated gene expression for Netrins or their receptors.
source: Some TCGA HGSOC cases display elevated gene expression for Netrins or their receptors, but only rare cases display low expression (Figure 7; Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Figure 7—figure supplement 1B shows oncoprint with some cases showing high mRNA expression for Netrin pathway genes.

claim: Netrin signaling in HGSOC is retained despite high copy number variation.
source: This suggests that Netrin signaling in HGSOC is retained despite high copy number variation in this cancer type and there is occasional overexpression.
evidence: This is inferred from the rare deletions and occasional overexpression of Netrin pathway genes in TCGA data.

claim: High level expression of Netrin-1 and -3 correlates with significantly shorter overall survival in HGSOC patients.
source: In agreement with our experimental data that multiple Netrin ligands can contribute to spheroid survival in HGSOC (Figure 5A and B), sorting cases by high level expression of Netrin-1 and –3 ligands reveals a significantly shorter overall survival compared to cases with low level expression and this trend is also evident in the cases that only overexpress Netrin-3 (Figure 7A).
evidence: Figure 7A shows Kaplan-Meier survival curves with significantly shorter overall survival for patients with high NTN1/NTN3 or NTN3 expression (logrank test).

claim: Overexpression of Netrin-1 or -3 increases OVCAR8 cell survival in dormant spheroid culture conditions.
source: This data indicates that overexpression of either Netrin-1 or –3 increases OVCAR8 cell survival in dormant spheroid culture conditions.
evidence: Figure 7C shows increased viability in OVCAR8 cells overexpressing Netrin-1 or -3 compared to vector control in suspension culture.

claim: Elevated survival in Netrin overexpressing cells is explained by an increase in abundance of individual spheroids.
source: Examination of fixed spheroids isolated from this experiment further indicates that elevated survival in this experiment is explained by an increase in abundance of individual spheroids that overexpress either Netrin-1 or –3 (Figure 7D).
evidence: Figure 7D shows increased number and size of spheroids in Netrin-1 or -3 overexpressing cells compared to control.

claim: High level Netrin expression confers oncogenic properties on HGSOC cells in suspension culture.
source: High level expression correlates with poor outcome and in suspension culture, overexpression confers oncogenic properties on HGSOC cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the increased survival in suspension culture and correlation with poor patient outcomes.

claim: Tumor nodules were detected with increased abundance on the diaphragm, liver, and mesometrium in mice xenografted with Netrin overexpressing cells compared to control.
source: In contrast, tumor nodules were detected with increased abundance on the diaphragm, the liver, and mesenteries that support the uterus (mesometrium; Figure 8B).
evidence: Figure 8B petal plots show increased frequency of tumor nodules in diaphragm, liver, and mesometrium for Netrin overexpressing cells compared to control.

claim: The quantity of tumor nodules was increased in Netrin overexpressing xenografts compared to OVCAR8 control cells.
source: In addition to more frequent disease spread to these locations caused by Netrin overexpressing cells, we note that the quantity of nodules was also increase in comparison with OVCAR8 control cells (Figure 8C–F).
evidence: Figure 8D and 8F show increased number of tumor nodules in mesometrium and liver for Netrin overexpressing cells compared to control.

claim: Netrin-1 and -3 are present in the local tumor microenvironment of xenograft lesions.
source: Lastly, Netrin-1 and –3 histochemical staining confirms its presence in the local tumor microenvironment (Figure 8G and H).
evidence: Figure 8G and 8H show immunohistochemical staining for Netrin-1 and -3 in tumor nodules from xenografts.

claim: Netrin signaling improves cell viability in spheroid aggregates in vivo leading to increased disease spread.
source: The similarity of increased tumor nodules seen in xenografts and elevated spheroid formation and viability seen in culture suggests that Netrin signaling improves cell viability in spheroid aggregates in vivo leading to increased disease spread.
evidence: This is inferred from the parallel observations of increased spheroid survival in culture and increased tumor nodules in xenografts with Netrin overexpression.

claim: Dormant HGSOC cells are characterized by similar metabolic changes, EMT, and cytokine signaling as dormant cancer cells from other disease sites.
source: Dormant HGSOC cells are characterized by similar metabolic changes, EMT, and cytokine signaling as dormant cancer cells from other disease sites (Sosa et al., 2014; Shepherd and Dick, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Sosa et al., 2014 and Shepherd and Dick, 2022.

claim: AMPK-LKB1 signaling induces autophagy in dormant HGSOC cells.
source: Mechanisms that mediate their dormant properties include AMPK-LKB1 signaling that induces autophagy (Peart et al., 2015; Buensuceso et al., 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Peart et al., 2015 and Buensuceso et al., 2020.

claim: STAT3 and FAK mediate survival and chemoresistance in dormant HGSOC cells.
source: STAT3 and FAK for survival and chemoresistance (Chen et al., 2017b; Diaz Osterman et al., 2019)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2017b and Diaz Osterman et al., 2019.

claim: DYRK1A signaling arrests proliferation in dormant HGSOC cells.
source: and DYRK1A signaling to arrest proliferation (MacDonald et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to MacDonald et al., 2017.

claim: Netrin-1 is the most studied Netrin and its misregulation in cancer leads to pro-survival signals.
source: Netrin-1 is the most studied and its misregulation in cancer leads to pro-survival signals (Arakawa, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Arakawa, 2004.

claim: Netrin interactions with DCC and UNC5 homologs convert pro-death signals by these dependence receptors to survival signals.
source: Netrin interactions with DCC and UNC5 homologs (UNC5H, UNC5A-D) convert pro-death signals by these dependence receptors to survival signals (Brisset et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Brisset et al., 2021.

claim: Netrin signals through PI3K-AKT and ERK-MAPK participate in orientation decisions in development by providing guidance cues.
source: Netrin signals through PI3K-AKT and ERK-MAPK are known to participate in orientation decisions in development by providing guidance cues (Forcet et al., 2002; Larrieu-Lahargue et al., 2010; Yin et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Forcet et al., 2002; Larrieu-Lahargue et al., 2010; and Yin et al., 2017.

claim: Loss of Netrin ligand binding leads DCC or UNC5H to stimulate dephosphorylation of DAPK1 that sends pro-death signals.
source: while loss of ligand binding leads DCC or UNC5H to stimulate dephosphorylation of DAPK1 that sends pro-death signals (Llambi et al., 2005; Castets et al., 2009)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Llambi et al., 2005 and Castets et al., 2009.

claim: The gene encoding DCC is frequently deleted in cancer.
source: The gene encoding DCC is frequently deleted in cancer (Arakawa, 2004)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Arakawa, 2004.

claim: Netrin-1 blocking antibodies are in Phase II clinical trials for endometrial and cervical carcinomas to inhibit metastatic growth.
source: and Netrin-1 blocking antibodies are in Phase II clinical trials for endometrial and cervical carcinomas to inhibit metastatic growth (Brisset et al., 2021)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Brisset et al., 2021.

claim: Alternative receptors for Netrins such as NEO, DSCAM, and Integrins mediate their signals.
source: Alternative receptors for Netrins such as NEO, DSCAM, and Integrins also mediate their signals (Mehlen et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Mehlen et al., 2011.

claim: Functional roles for Netrin-3, -4, and -5 are still relatively unexplored compared to Netrin-1.
source: Lastly, functional roles for Netrin-3,–4, and –5 are still relatively unexplored compared to Netrin-1 (Bruikman et al., 2019)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Bruikman et al., 2019.

claim: Netrin expression patterns suggest roles in advanced forms of some cancers.
source: although their expression patterns suggest roles in advanced forms of some cancers (Jiang et al., 2021)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Jiang et al., 2021.

claim: HGSOC spheroids are ideal to search for survival dependencies specific to dormant cells.
source: This suggests that HGSOC spheroids are ideal to search for survival dependencies specific to dormant cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that HGSOC spheroids display characteristics of dormancy similar to other cancer types.

claim: HGSOC is the deadliest gynecologic malignancy, accounting for more than 70% of cases.
source: HGSOC is the deadliest gynecologic malignancy, accounting for more than 70% of cases (Lheureux et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lheureux et al., 2019.

claim: Metastatic spread in HGSOC is facilitated by multicellular clusters of tumor cells called spheroids that are shed into the peritoneal cavity and disseminate to nearby organs.
source: Metastatic spread is facilitated by multicellular clusters of tumor cells, called spheroids, that are shed into the peritoneal cavity and disseminate to nearby organs (Lengyel, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lengyel, 2010.

claim: The non-proliferative state of spheroid cells renders them chemoresistant and contributes to disease recurrence.
source: The non-proliferative state of spheroid cells renders them chemoresistant and contributes to disease recurrence, emphasizing the need to understand the biology of these cells (Bowtell et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Bowtell et al., 2015.

claim: Disseminated cancer cells often occupy specific cellular niches in perivascular space or in bone marrow.
source: Disseminated cells often occupy specific cellular niches in perivascular space or in bone marrow (Goddard et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Goddard et al., 2018.

claim: Dormant cancer cells adopt catabolic metabolism.
source: They adopt catabolic metabolism (Massagué and Ganesh, 2021)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Massagué and Ganesh, 2021.

claim: Dormant cancer cells withdraw from the cell cycle.
source: and withdraw from the cell cycle (Phan and Croucher, 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Phan and Croucher, 2020.

claim: Stem like phenotypes and epithelial to mesenchymal transition characterize the biology of dormant cancer cells.
